correctness.rationale: The exactly defined six unordered matching-pair types have capped multiplicities 0,1,>=2 that suffice to determine every successor-neighbor test and update. All 707 feasible capped signatures were enumerated with ordered vertex-state tracking, proving F^5=F^2 for any n>=3. A symbolic labelled-pair exponential generating function gives the six integer counts, independently corroborated by direct vertex simulation of 5,380,749 initial states for n=3..7. The proof excludes n=2 and makes no claim for four colors.

value.rationale: The complement of a perfect matching is a canonical near-complete, strongly regular graph family. The exact all-state two-step periodic-entry identity and six labelled basin classes quantify rapid periodic locking and exponential consensus rarity beyond the known consensus-only diameter bound. The graph/rule-specific complete orbit census is a natural invariant for this dynamical family, not a contrived slice.
